items.title: Universal 3.5 Pro Demo: Smarter Speech-to-Text with Contextual Awareness
items.summary:
Universal 3.5 Pro: Smarter Speech-to-Text with Contextual Awareness 🧠🎙️

In this demo, we walk through the new contextual awareness capabilities of Universal 3.5 Pro—and how they dramatically improve transcription accuracy, especially for voice agents.

What's covered:
         🔹 Contextual prompting: Pass a description of your audio ("cardiology consultation about chest pain") and accuracy improves within that domain. The more specific the prompt, the better the results.
         🔹 Key terms with context: Key terms are no longer applied blindly. Tell the model what a term is ("The user's name is Zachary Klebanoff") and it won't force the term onto acoustically similar phrases.
         🔹 Dynamic mid-call prompt updates: Update the prompt in real time via the API (e.g., after a tool call identifies the caller) to boost accuracy as the conversation unfolds.
         🔹 Conversation context (agent context): The model retains previous transcriptions in the session and accepts your voice agent's LLM-generated responses as context. If the agent asks "What's your email?", the model expects an email next — without over-biasing. We've seen significant word error rate reductions on voice agent datasets, even in poor audio conditions.

Watch the full demo, including a live customer support scenario with dynamic context updates and mid-call tool calls.

items.title: ARC-AGI-3 winning team - Millennia of minds, compressed into words.
items.summary:
Tim Scarfe travels to Zurich to sit down with the Tufa Labs ARC-AGI-3 team — founder Benjamin Crouzier, with Jeroen Cottaar, Dries Smit, Stefano Viel and Michal Tesnar — to work out what their leaderboard-topping system does and what the benchmark is really testing.

The cut opens on the games: a walkthrough of the Locksmith game, where you read the rules of an unfamiliar world straight from raw frames. ARC-AGI-3 makes ARC interactive and agentic, so the model has to *discover* the goal rather than transduce a static grid. It stays easy for humans and breaks LLMs, and it runs through everything that follows. Dries traces his StochasticGoose preview win — brute force that only searched actions which changed the frame — and why it collapsed once the organisers added action-efficiency scoring and unseen games.

Induction and transduction run through the middle of the conversation — how much of an answer is really priors leaking back the moment a model recognises a maze. The abstraction mountain, and Tim's case that LLMs reach the right answer through fractured, entangled representations — performance, not competence. Whether transformers plan at all or just fake it well enough. Why the score really measures action efficiency, not games solved, and why agents lock onto the wrong goal and cannot climb back out.

Crouzier closes on the Tufa Labs thesis — a small lab against the giants, the bitter lesson against hand-built harnesses, and safety — and Tim ties it back to Kenneth Stanley, deep constraints, and creativity as competence.

Disclosure: Tufa Labs sponsors MLST.

items.title: CoreWeave ARIA: The autoresearch loop for continuous improvement
items.summary:
Meet CoreWeave ARIA, the AI Research and Iteration Agent that continuously improves your model and agent. In this demo, you will see how ARIA runs the full autoresearch loop. By continuously forming hypotheses, running experiments, evaluating results, and executing the best next actions, AIRA creates an autonomous research loop that helps models and agents improve while you focus on the problems that require human judgment. 

Get started: https://docs.wandb.ai/aria/overview
